s.en: packet filtering and NAT in the kernel (Linux firewall)
s.es: filtra paquetes y hace NAT en el núcleo (cortafuegos de Linux)

syn: iptables [-t table] {-A|-C|-D|-V} chain rule-specification ⏎ ip6tables [-t table] {-A|-C|-D|-V} chain rule-specification ⏎ iptables [-t table] -I chain [rulenum] rule-specification ⏎ iptables [-t table] -R chain rulenum rule-specification ⏎ iptables [-t table] -D chain rulenum ⏎ iptables [-t table] -S [chain [rulenum]]

tip.es: Antes de «-P INPUT DROP» o «-F» por SSH, asegúrate de tener una regla que permita tu propia sesión (ESTABLISHED) o te quedarás fuera.
tip.en: Before "-P INPUT DROP" or "-F" over SSH, make sure you have a rule allowing your own session (ESTABLISHED) or you will lock yourself out.

o.es: AÑADE una regla al FINAL de la cadena (INPUT, OUTPUT, FORWARD…).
o.en: APPEND a rule at the END of the chain (INPUT, OUTPUT, FORWARD…).

o.es: INSERTA una regla al principio (o en la posición indicada).
o.en: INSERT a rule at the beginning (or at the given position).

o.es: BORRA una regla (por especificación o por número).
o.en: DELETE a rule (by specification or by number).

o.es: Reemplaza una regla por su número.
o.en: Replace a rule by its number.

o.es: Lista las reglas.
o.en: List the rules.

o.es: Muestra las reglas como comandos reutilizables.
o.en: Print the rules as reusable commands.

o.es: VACÍA todas las reglas de la cadena (o de todas).
o.en: FLUSH all rules of the chain (or all of them).

o.es: Borra una cadena vacía definida por el usuario.
o.en: Delete a user-defined empty chain.

o.es: Crea una cadena nueva.
o.en: Create a new user-defined chain.

o.es: Política por defecto: ACCEPT o DROP.
o.en: Set the default policy: ACCEPT or DROP.

o.es: Pone a cero los contadores.
o.en: Zero the packet and byte counters.

o.es: Tabla: filter (por defecto), nat, mangle, raw.
o.en: Table: filter (default), nat, mangle, raw.

o.es: Protocolo: tcp, udp, icmp, all.
o.en: Protocol: tcp, udp, icmp, all.

o.es: Dirección de origen (admite /máscara).
o.en: Source address (/mask allowed).

o.es: Dirección de destino.
o.en: Destination address.

o.es: Interfaz de entrada.
o.en: Name of an interface via which a packet was received.

o.es: Interfaz de salida.
o.en: Name of an interface via which a packet is going to be sent.

o.es: Puerto de destino (con -p tcp/udp).
o.en: Destination port (with -p tcp/udp).

o.es: Puerto de origen.
o.en: Source port.

o.es: Qué hacer con el paquete: ACCEPT (dejar pasar), DROP (descartar en silencio), REJECT (rechazar con aviso), LOG, DNAT, SNAT, MASQUERADE…
o.en: What to do with the packet: ACCEPT, DROP (silently discard), REJECT (refuse with notice), LOG, DNAT, SNAT, MASQUERADE…

o.es: Carga un módulo de coincidencia (state, conntrack, multiport, limit…).
o.en: Load a match module (state, conntrack, multiport, limit…).

o.es: Con -m state: NEW, ESTABLISHED, RELATED, INVALID.
o.en: With -m state: NEW, ESTABLISHED, RELATED, INVALID.

o.es: Con -m conntrack: estado de la conexión.
o.en: With -m conntrack: connection state.

o.es: Con DNAT: nueva dirección:puerto de destino.
o.en: With DNAT: new destination address:port.

o.es: Con REDIRECT: puerto al que se redirige.
o.en: With REDIRECT: port to redirect to.

o.es: Muestra direcciones y puertos numéricos.
o.en: Numeric output of addresses and ports.

o.es: Muestra contadores e interfaces.
o.en: Verbose output (counters and interfaces).

o.es: Numera las reglas al listarlas (para poder borrarlas por número).
o.en: Add line numbers to the rules when listing.

o.es: Comprueba si existe una regla.
o.en: Check whether a rule exists.

o.es: Espera el bloqueo de xtables.
o.en: Wait for the xtables lock.
Rename the user specified chain to the user supplied name. This is cosmetic, and has no effect on the structure of the table.
Help. Give a (currently very brief) description of the command syntax.

This option has no effect in iptables and iptables-restore. If a rule using the -4 option is inserted with (and only with) ip6tables-restore, it will be silently ignored. Any other uses will throw an error. This option allows IPv4 and IPv6 rules in a single rule file for use with both iptables-restore and ip6tables-restore.

If a rule using the -6 option is inserted with (and only with) iptables-restore, it will be silently ignored. Any other uses will throw an error. This option allows IPv4 and IPv6 rules in a single rule file for use with both iptables-restore and ip6tables-restore. This option has no effect in ip6tables and ip6tables-restore.

This specifies that the processing should continue in a user specified chain. Unlike with the --jump option, RETURN will not continue processing in this chain but instead in the chain that called us via --jump.
This enables the administrator to initialize the packet and byte counters of a rule (during INSERT, APPEND, REPLACE operations).
Show program version and the kernel API used.

Expand numbers. Display the exact value of the packet and byte counters, instead of only the rounded number in K's (multiples of 1000), M's (multiples of 1000K) or G's (multiples of 1000M). This option is only relevant for the -L command.
When adding or inserting rules into a chain, use command to load any necessary modules (targets, match extensions, etc).
